episodes.title: Trust Me: The False Prophet With Dr. Christine Marie: Trauma Bonds, Coercive Control, And How To Leave
episodes.description:
In this powerful episode of The Danette May Show, I sit down again with Dr. Christine Marie from Trust Me: The False Prophet for a deeper conversation on trauma bonds, coercive control, narcissistic abuse patterns, and why leaving a controlling relationship or system can feel so confusing. We talk about how the “good times” can become part of the abuse cycle, how intermittent reinforcement keeps people emotionally attached, and why fear can sometimes be mistaken for love when the nervous system is living in survival mode.
This conversation is about awareness, safety, and hope. Dr. Christine shares practical ways to begin seeing the truth more clearly, from tracking negative and positive interactions to listening to your body’s signals, understanding the power and control wheel, recognizing coercion, and creating a safety plan if you are unsure how to leave. My hope is that this episode reminds you that you are not alone, there is no shame in what you have experienced, and your voice, intuition, freedom, and self-trust can be reclaimed.
This episode is an independent conversation and commentary related to themes discussed around Trust Me: The False Prophet and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Netflix.

episodes.title: Trust Me: The False Prophet With Dr. Christine Marie: Coercive Control, Cult Psychology, And Healing, Part 1 Continued
episodes.description:
In this powerful continuation of my conversation with Dr. Christine Marie from Netflix’s Trust Me: The False Prophet, we go deeper into the psychology of coercive control, brainwashing, religious trauma, and survivor healing. Dr. Christine shares what it was like to be part of the documentary without having creative control, how she built trust with members of the FLDS community through a harm reduction approach, and how the filming unexpectedly became part of a much larger story involving Sam Bateman, survivor courage, and the predator playbook.
We also talk about the belief gaps around Warren Jeffs, what it means to create a safe “Switzerland” space for people in and out of high-control religions, and why coercive control laws matter so deeply when protecting victims and children. This episode is a powerful reminder that healing can happen when we stop judging, start helping, and turn trauma into triumph.
This episode is an independent conversation and commentary related to themes discussed around Trust Me: The False Prophet and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Netflix.
